notes.title: Status update
notes.notes:
Hello everybody!

We know many of you eagerly await news about the next patch and a plan for the following updates. We're sorry to hear that Yacht Mechanic Simulator failed to meet expectations. We, as a publisher, humbly apologize for letting this happen. Going forward, we must do better and we will do better.

Sadly, we don't have any good news to share at the moment. To this day, we have only received one functional patch from the dev team and it surely didn't fix all of the issues you face. Since the last patch went live, the developer didn't share with us any information regarding the scale of the next patch and we didn't receive any ETA for it either. Because of this, we, sadly, can't answer your questions regarding the contents or the release date of the next patch - we don't have this information either. 

We didn't inform you of the delay in new patches because we expected them to roll out faster. But it's nearly a month after the release, and we owe you sincere and clear communication. So, here it is.

That said, we are trying to get things settled with the developer so that you don't have to wait for the patch any longer. Simultaneously, we're looking into other solutions.

We want Yacht Mechanic Simulator to be in a state that you, the players, will deem acceptable. We're doing what we can for you to receive the support you deserve. But this might still take some time, depending on how the current situation evolves. 

Hopefully, more patches will start rolling out soon. We are dedicated to improving this game and we'll keep looking for a solution to your problems for as long as it takes. Until then, thank you for your patience.

Best 
Image Power team

notes.title: Important community update
notes.notes:
Hi guys,

It’s Yacht’s main producer here. Day 1 was quite tough. We started with a positive attitude while launching the game but pretty soon it came clear that some things didn’t go well.

First of all, I’m sorry that we didn’t deliver the top quality on launch. We are a small team and it is safe to say that we were too confident with development process/testing. We tried to do our best but that doesn’t always work, right? We owe you an explanation and apologize to those of you who experienced serious issues with the game. 

It seems that at least some of you experienced and are still experiencing major issues with our game. We are now focused on patching YMS. We are now compelling the list of crucial bugs, and soon we will enter the phase of fixing. That said:

[h3]You may expect patches coming your way. We are now working hard to deliver it as soon as possible. I want it to be properly tested and solid. This is our responsibility and we treat it very, very seriously. We owe you that and we fully recognize this fact.[/h3]

With that said, I wanted to thank everyone who willingly contributed to our game. It is priceless that some folks spent their time talking to us and reporting to us. We are in your debt!!! And to all of you who play and enjoy the game, we are also so happy to see it.

We humbly accept negatives  – we don’t blame anyone but ourselves.[b] If you however like the game and you haven’t experienced any serious issues – your positive review would mean the world to us now. It would make our current work more meaningful. [/b]

Last but not least, please use this Steam forum thread if you want to report any technical/gameplay bugs: https://steamcommunity.com/app/1263620/discussions/1/3453716250587111209/  

Thank you for your support!

Punch Punk Games (dev) & Image Power (publisher)

notes.title: State of the game & things to come - Devlog
notes.notes:
[h2]Ahoy virtual mechanics and yacht lovers![/h2]

As you now know, [url=https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/1263620/view/3094530081462837424]Yacht Mechanic Simulator is due next year[/url]. However, aside from some necessary polishing and the new features we want to add, the game is mostly finished. This devlog will go more in-depth into what is ready and what is still planned before the release.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37207957/3b3fab081354e6d07964a2076951717b2c8a751f.gif[/img]
[i]Large yachts in testing[/i]

First and foremost, [b]all yachts are finished[/b] and playable. Instead of implementing a larger number of small yachts, we decided to put more emphasis on making a few larger vessels, arriving at a total of nine different ships. Of course, every yacht has a lot of differents elements to change or fix. Thanks to the random nature of contracts that the player can take, there is a ton of variety, especially on the bigger vessels.

Moreover, there is a functional tutorial as well as a simple [b]campaign mode[/b]. In the campaign, the player progressively unlocks more yachts to work on, as they amass more funds. Transition to a higher tier (with bigger and more expensive yachts) requires payments to a bank, which depend on the progress a player has made. After finishing the campaign, there is also a free mode, where you can do whatever you want. Just don't go bankrupt ;)

In terms of added gameplay elements, again, all of the essentials are ready. If you test a ship on the open waters and crash it into some rocks, you will have to fix a hole you made. Sometimes, clients can also request similar repairs. These take multiple steps to complete before the hull is properly fixed.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37207957/309f7c1cc0fe726a59eece674d3b5e44441df188.gif[/img]
[i]The final step in fixing a damaged hull[/i]

But there are some gameplay elements that were requested by players and testers alike. We acknowledge that additional features will make the game more enjoyable and we are in the process of picking the ones that will be added in the next few months. We almost finished picking them but there are a few that we are still deliberating on.

One of them is the [b]ability to fix broken parts[/b]. Right now, if you find a damaged element on one of the ships, you have to remove it, purchase a new one, and install it. However, many players and testers suggested the addition of a mode that lets you fix any broken parts. This would create a lot of new possibilities. For instance, you could fix a broken element instead of purchasing a replacement. Or you could purchase used parts from the store, fix them, and use install them as new additions to a yacht for some extra money.

Another highly requested feature is a [b]sonar [/b]that helps you [b]find things to fix or clean[/b]. The way it would work is simple - when the player presses a button, everything that needs their attention is highlighted for a moment, even when it's behind a wall or furniture. This feature could make it easier to figure out what you need to do. A lot of first time players ask for such addition. The truth is, people unaccustomed to yacht repairs sometimes have a hard time finding broken parts, especially on larger yachts. We already have an outline that informs the player if something is damaged or not. But adding a sonar to guide people through the many rooms on bigger yachts could be a big quality of life improvement.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37207957/23a8cd5ca94bff9dfbe10981bf983d3ba4a046e0.gif[/img]
[i]New shop UI that lets you find matching items easily[/i]

[b]We want to hear your input![/b] What do you think about the two features described above? Do you believe that they could have a big impact on your experience? Or perhaps there is something else that you really, really wish was added? Please let us know in the comments!

If you have any additional questions regarding the state of the game or our plans, drop them in the comments or [url=https://discord.gg/wnX4tvhASg]on our Discord server [/url]and we'll do our best to answer them!

[b]Best regards,
Image Power team[/b]

notes.title: New yacht, new mechanics, and Career mode - Devlog
notes.notes:
[h2]Ahoy virtual mechanics and yacht lovers![/h2]

We admit, it has been some time since our last devlog. But as we reach the later stages of development, we're ready to start discussing some of the recent major changes we've made to the game. Buckle up, this will be a long one!

Let's start by discussing the thing you're probably the most curious about - [b]the Career Mode[/b]! Yacht Mechanic Simulator 2021 was always meant to have an engaging campaign with natural player progression. You will begin your journey with limited funds and access to only some of the cheaper yacht models. As you start earning more money, you will gradually gain access to bigger, more impressive, and more expensive vessels. Moreover, you can charge a premium for redecorating a yacht completely - the more work you do, the more valuable your boat will be. It won't be long before you get a chance to experience a short preview of the campaign mode so stay tuned for updates!

Speaking of yachts, every month we've been adding a new yacht model to the game. We already have quite a few of them finished and most of the armada is ready to sail! [b]Check out our most recent addition below[/b]:

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37207957/1a228bd7978f3feada92e100c44fedbb8653a198.jpg[/img]

Meanwhile, there was a lot of work on expanding the audio side of this project. In order to maximize immersion, we've implemented [b]dozens of new sounds and noises[/b], in addition to tweaking the ones already present in the game. All of the new sounds are also scalable, meaning that their intensity will differ depending on the situation.

We're also[b] improving the economy[/b]. This wasn't our main concern at the time when our demo was released, since it was mostly a proof of concept and a bit of sandbox-y fun. But now that the Career Mode is looming over the horizon, it's about time to make some changes - and so we did! All of the prices in YMS2021 have been completely rebalanced. Additionally, there are new sources of revenue as well as new expenses to take into account. Even your trusty tools might show signs of wear and tear over time.

Finally, you're prayers have been answered and YMS2021 is getting a [b]proper inventory system[/b]! No more selling and repurchasing cables that are in the way. Now you can just put them aside and use them at a later date.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37207957/32ce2dc322111a2d1aebbed40ff748f8c856e3e1.gif[/img]

Aside from all of that, we're fixing various bugs, either the ones that you reported or the ones that our QA team spotted. We're preparing a new, bigger version to share with you and our current priority is to make sure that it plays smoothly. Speaking of which, there is an announcement we need to make - as of today, it's no longer possible to play our public demo.

The reason is simple - our demo was getting rather old. We published it during our Kickstarter campaign and it hasn't changed since then, as we've been working on the main game. At this stage, our demo shows some outdated mechanics and features bugs that are long gone by now. It's about time we say goodbye. Of course, our backers will still keep their access but the demo will no longer be publically downloadable. Worry not, you will get something [b]much cooler[/b] this summer! :goldenstarDPW:

That is all for this devlog. This is just the tip of the iceberg though, as there are many, many more things we did since our last update. We will be back with more news next month and that's a promise! Meanwhile, if there's anything you want to ask, feel free to reach out to us on our [url=https://discord.gg/6YMnDUtBXc]Discord server[/url]



Yacht Mechanic Simulator 2021 is, as the name implies, releasing in 2021 so it won't be long now! Don't wait and add it to your Wishlist on Steam:

notes.title: Devlog III or “how to make it better?”
notes.notes:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37207957/338ba9798c0268e3f232b7757ecc18a367a47dd9.png[/img]

[h2]Hello everyone![/h2]

We just started a new year, which means a new update for [b]Yacht Mechanic Simulator[/b]. Many changes will come to the game this time, so set your sails and hold tight! We’re going on an adventure! However, if this is the first our devlog you came across, we highly recommend you take a look at the previous ones - about [url=https://steamcommunity.com/games/1263620/announcements/detail/2888454251873353952]creating an enjoyable experience[/url] and about [url=https://steamcommunity.com/games/1263620/announcements/detail/2936874288619839596]sailing mechanics development[/url].

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37207957/51e94b03ad5eb0f87bb44e34a305313ff4419046.gif[/img]

We’re going to start our journey with an overview of the navigation system. After the last [b]Steam Game Festival[/b], we received a great amount of feedback from the players, which prompted us to completely redo the camera settings. Earlier, during the yacht renovation stage, our game used predefined viewing angles, which sometimes made it difficult for people to get a good view of the part of the boat they were working on. [b]We decided to replace the automatic camera with free control so that each player can adjust the perspective to their own preferences and convenience.[/b] After those changes, some in-game mechanics ended up being easier to implement, while others became more challenging. For instance, the deck washing feature - it took some effort to combine the new free movement of the camera with the way some tools are controlled.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37207957/6b9448fb06b68d28628af2b8b87b857ac4b3acfc.gif[/img]

[b]Renovating yachts is supposed to be fun and it’s our job to make sure you don’t get bored easily![/b] When doing research on real boats, we were surprised by how many elements we could tinker with. Because of this, we decided to include more interactive objects. We believe that giving players a chance to explore all nooks and crannies of yachts will make them more likely to return to their boats and discover something completely different each time. Such changes prompted us to implement interactive buttons into the game world, instead of leaving them as part of the UI. Last, but not least - we prepared a new cutscene for your first boat launch. From now on, the return of the Prestige yacht to the ocean can be experienced in a unique video clip!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37207957/fa1b3722d4ccde47de164e2a7141d36eb82f2075.gif[/img]

Oh, and probably you've already noticed some changes on our Steam page! Yes, we changed a name of the game by adding [b]"2021"[/b] at the end. Now, there should be no doubt that the release of Yacht Mechanic Simulator is not very far away ;) Stay tuned!

That’s it for now! We're absolutely excited to see what the future holds for our game and we’re extremely happy to see you becoming part of this project as well!

Be seeing you!

[b]Cheers, 
Image Power Team[/b]

https://store.steampowered.com/app/1263620/Yacht_Mechanic_Simulator/

notes.title: Devlog II or “are we gonna sail?”
notes.notes:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37207957/ef354871d0bcfee0f8196bb6c99cbfea6a0e1af2.png[/img]

[h1]Hello everyone![/h1]

:landlessboat: We’re finally back with [b]another update[/b] and this time we’re going to talk about sailing.

If you’re interested in the development process of [b]Yacht Mechanic Simulator[/b], we highly recommend you take a look at our [url=https://steamcommunity.com/games/1263620/announcements/detail/2888454251873353952]first devlog[/url] to learn more about the challenge of creating a believable experience and adapting real-life mechanics to the game.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37207957/bfdfe1242af8fdba56dec61b91061b4b04eef08f.png[/img]

Right now we are working on sailing mechanics. [b]Our ultimate goal is to make the very first boat run an unforgettable and most credible moment.[/b] During internal tests, our testers suggested several solutions that would make it a pleasant part of the gameplay. First of all, we improved the throttle valve effectiveness, which keeps the boat at speed instead of slowing it down. Secondly - we tweaked the UI - from now on, it will display information about what stage of the inspection the player is at. In addition, during the cruise, we will be able to time the boat on a water slalom course.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37207957/2fdba9da812f67cd52a150bc9af772ff91d47d49.png[/img]

Another thing to work on (literally!) is [b]engine replacement[/b]. As we mentioned in the previous devlog - one of the biggest challenges ahead of us was the engine replacement mechanics.  Today we can happily announce that everything works as expected and this aspect of the game is officially completed. We can also confirm that a model of a [b]third yacht[/b] has made it to the game and is already waiting in the harbor for a mechanic to repair it. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37207957/21f637e57b95c97b5b2cea5dc5f7783c558dd978.png[/img]

Thanks to the Yacht Mechanic Simulator’s presence at the [b]Steam Game Festival[/b], we received huge feedback from players. Direct cooperation with the community is something really valuable for us because it gives us the confidence that we are providing you with a product that fully meets your expectations. Moreover, we received many helpful messages, which allowed us to fix some bugs that appeared in the game only in specific situations and, despite numerous tests, still remained undetected. Thanks to that we can offer players a simulator that will engage them and won’t disrupt their immersion with errors.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37207957/5b5a4cc7ddeb03218c245dafe39fba394d25d507.png[/img]

:landlessboat: That’s it for now. There is still a long way to go, but we are definitely one step closer to the finish line. 

Until we meet again!

[b]Cheers, 
Image Power Team[/b]

https://store.steampowered.com/app/1263620/Yacht_Mechanic_Simulator/

notes.title: Devlog or “what's happening lately?”
notes.notes:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37207957/9d81912e4e1ba7231e8732887dab7b895b630b36.png[/img]

☀️ Hello everyone! ☀️

You’re often asking about the progress on Yacht Mechanic Simulator. [b]We’ll be more than happy to answer those questions today![/b]

We’re working hard to provide you with an enjoyable experience of bringing old yachts to life. We have two models fully finished and we’re preparing more, to give you a variety of boats to choose from. Actually, we wouldn’t be surprised if we tweaked the first two, as we come back to them with a fresh mind later! 

When it comes to the overall look of the game, we already achieved great quality. However, we’re perfectionists at heart, so we continue working on this part as well, until we are honestly satisfied with the looks. This is going to be a realistic game; sadly, we won’t be able to give you the feel of the sea breeze, but we can help your imagination to do the job. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37207957/f0e34936b9ae4ccff576357149c0aa707f25a4b8.jpg[/img]

Speaking of ideas - there are some parts of the game where the gameplay must speak for itself, instead of forcing you to fill in the blanks with your imagination. We pay great attention to even the smallest details, to make sure that the direct work on the yacht won’t be clunky. With that in mind, we already finished most of the mechanics and animations.

In real life, screwing parts has its physics and those can’t be altered. Otherwise, the whole construction won’t hold together for a long time. To develop the same mechanics, we watched closely what the process of fixing real boats looks like and then we successfully transferred it into the game. Sometimes imitation is the best way of doing something right.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37207957/f8ad5412160555e8cf22b1756161357952942bc0.jpg[/img]

Developing the deck cleaning mechanic was really time consuming, because of how complex it is. You will have to get rid of the old furniture, walls, floors, lights. It will also be a good idea to refresh the whole interior before you start arranging it from scratch and modernising it. It does sound like a step-by-step process and we had to make sure that each of those steps is working properly.

You know what kept us awake at night? Side-washing the yacht! You’ll get to use a hose with water under high pressure and, believe us, animating it was a real challenge. Water interacts  differently with different surfaces, so we needed to adjust the animations to make sure the process feels natural.

The mechanic of exchanging parts is also finished, as we’re working simultaneously on other games and we’re trying to use similar methods across titles from our portfolio. What was also very helpful was our own experience with yachts - all this combined helped us make this mechanic very realistic. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37207957/efae93c53cd27c35c5fbfe788c1395fd6452fc1b.jpg[/img]

With all of those features finished, we can focus on the remaining elements of the process. Mechanically, the biggest challenge for us, so far, was the yacht’s engine and replacing it, so we keep on polishing that part.  

Phew… That’s a lot!
It was just a brief recap on some of the changes, but we already can’t wait to share the future updates with you. It is even possible that we will have a cool surprise for you next time 😉 Stay tuned!

[b]Cheers,
Image Power Team[/b]

https://store.steampowered.com/app/1263620/Yacht_Mechanic_Simulator/

notes.title: Yacht Mechanic Simulator - FAQ
notes.notes:
[h3]When is the game releasing? I want to fix and drive the boats NOW![/h3]
Please be patient for a bit longer. We will keep you updated on the development of Yacht Mechanic Simulator and when we’ll be ready to announce the release date, you’ll be the first to know!

[h3]Are you planning to release a demo of the game?[/h3]
If you all really want it, we can definitely think about it!

[h3]What can you actually do in the game? Paint the yachts? Install new furniture? What else?[/h3]
First of all, you can buy a crappy boat and fix it up. Clean it, wipe it, paint it, put in new equipment and fix whatever is broken. Once everything is nice and shiny, you can think about some visual tuning and finally put the yacht on sale to get money for new projects. You can also take on jobs and gain sailing ranks.

[h3]How will I be able to fix the boats? I don’t want to do a sloppy job…[/h3]
There’s nothing to be afraid of - the game will explain what each element does and what requires fixing. Give it a couple of tries and you’ll be a pro yacht mechanic!

[h3]I have a soul of an interior designer, so I want the interiors of my yachts to be stunning. Is that possible?[/h3]
Of course it’s possible - Yacht Mechanic Simulator is in a way like House Flipper, but with yachts. There are tens of elements waiting for you - railings, couches and chairs or even clocks.

[h3]What happens after I pimp my yacht?[/h3]
It depends what your goal was. If you had a fixing contract, your job is done. But if you want to put it up for auction, don’t hesitate and try to sell it for as much, as you can!

[h3]So how many yachts are there going to be in the game? How big are they going to be? You know, they may be small or big…[/h3]
Our goal is to put 12-15 boats in the game. They will differ in many aspects, including price - while you’ll be able to get the the cheapest and smallest boats even for $15-20k, the most expensive ships will cost up to 30 million dollars!

[h3]Alright, which boat will be the biggest?[/h3]
The biggest yacht in the game will be 33 meters long. That’ll require some work!

[b]Add Yacht Mechanic Simulator to wishlist: [/b]

notes.title: Hobbies and games that come together. Why Yacht Mechanic Simulator?
notes.notes:
It is wonderful to be passionate about something. Find an activity you enjoy doing and which enables you to try out and learn new things. It is great when you get to do it in your spare time, even better when it becomes your job, because you are basically doing what you love for a living. When we came up with the idea for Yacht Mechanic Simulator, we were mostly thinking about what we would like to play as a form of replacement, if got disconnected from our hobbies.

Being keen on something, combined with being a game developer is a perfect mix. You can make games about various topics, which at first may seem completely incompatible with virtual entertainment. It is thanks to the fact that you have enough knowledge on specific subjects, so you are able to use it and create good games, which reflect reality in their mechanics. Thanks to this expertise, you can familiarize the player with the best aspects of your interests.

Because of our interest in yachts and sailing (and making games!), we have decided to create a simulator that will give players the opportunity to look at this passion from the best perspective possible - professional. We were wondering, what we - yachts’ enthusiasts - would like to see in such game? Which part of the hobby lured us in the first place, when it was just beginning to develop? We wanted to be authentic and put existing processes into the game. Thanks to that, people who already know yachts well, will find themselves in familiar conditions and those playing for the first time will feel they are doing something close to reality, while having fun at the same time.

Yachts are wonderful vehicles, interesting both from the outside and the inside. They operate with the help of extensive machinery, so working on them will, for sure, delight many engineers. Their layouts are marvelous. No matter which size you choose, the designers always put their whole heart into the yachts’ appearance. They are able to take people on wonderful adventures, allowing them to visit magnificent places. They are associated with luxury, spending your free time in unusual places or simply being on vacation. Our goal for the players was not only to work on yachts and admire them , but also to feel the atmosphere around these machines, unmatched by anything else.

Making a game about something we know and like is a wonderful experience. We were given the opportunity to use our entire knowledge in order to create a game which will show other people how entertaining our hobby can be. We hope there will be many similar enthusiasts among our players, but we also believe that we will be able to spread our passion for yachts to other people.
